failure: Not a failure. Recording the escalation step that worked, because the brief's ladder currently stops at 'try a browser User-Agent' and that was not sufficient.
tried: Two of the four hosts that first returned HTTP 403 to a browser User-Agent alone went to HTTP 200 once --http1.1 was forced AND the full Chrome header set was sent: uaelegislation.gov.ae (403 -> 200, 72 KB) and parlzim.gov.zw (403 -> 200, 26 KB). The header set that made the difference: sec-ch-ua, sec-ch-ua-mobile, sec-ch-ua-platform, Upgrade-Insecure-Requests, Sec-Fetch-Dest, Sec-Fetch-Mode, Sec-Fetch-Site, Sec-Fetch-User, a realistic Accept, and Accept-Language. The same escalation did NOT rescue riigiteataja.ee or peraturan.bpk.go.id. Recommendation: add 'full Chrome header set plus --http1.1, not just the UA string' as step 1b of the ladder, before declaring a host blocked. Two further reusable tricks found in this batch: (1) zakon.rada.gov.ua serves only a record card at /laws/show/ID but the full consolidated text at /laws/show/ID/print; (2) laws.e-gov.go.jp is an SPA shell, but elaws.e-gov.go.jp/api/1/lawdata/LAWID returns the full statute as XML.
